channel.title: The QUBE Blog
channel.description: Plain-English reads on training, recovery and the research behind what goes in your glass.

item.title: Supplements for vertical jump: what research shows
item.description: Which supplements for vertical jump have research behind them? A 2025 network meta-analysis and a creatine meta-analysis, plus what they cannot tell you.

item.title: How to read a supplement label: an athlete's guide
item.description: How to read a supplement label as an athlete: what the Supplement Facts panel shows, where labels can miss, and why testing matters. Plain-English guide.

item.title: Creatine monohydrate vs HCl: which form is better?
item.description: Creatine monohydrate vs creatine HCl: a 2025 trial in 31 elite athletes and a 2011 review found no proof HCl is better. See what the studies show.

item.title: Creatine for female athletes: what research shows
item.description: Creatine for female athletes: what a 2025 systematic review, a 2020 safety meta-analysis and a 2021 review found, and where the evidence is still thin.

item.title: Creatine loading: do you need to load creatine?
item.description: Do you need creatine loading? A 1996 muscle biopsy study and two ISSN papers show 3 to 5 g a day gets you there, just slower. Here is the trade-off.

item.title: Magnesium for muscle cramps: what athletes should know
item.description: Does magnesium for muscle cramps work? A Cochrane review of 11 trials and a sports medicine review say the evidence is weak. Here is what athletes should know.

item.title: Supplements for vertical jump: what research shows
item.description: Does tart cherry help sleep? A 2025 systematic review and a small trial in elite athletes show promise, but the evidence is limited. Here is the breakdown.

item.title: When to take creatine: does timing really matter?
item.description: When to take creatine: before, after or any time? What a 2021 review and a pre vs post workout trial found, and why daily consistency matters.

item.title: Curcumin for muscle soreness: what studies show
item.description: Curcumin for muscle soreness: what a 2022 meta-analysis of 10 trials and a 2024 review found, what is still unclear, and where curcumin fits in QUBE.

item.title: Creatine and beta-alanine together: does it work?
item.description: Can you take creatine and beta-alanine together? What a 2025 systematic review found, what the ISSN says about each, and where the evidence stops.

item.title: Tart cherry for muscle soreness: what studies show
item.description: Does tart cherry help muscle soreness? Two meta-analyses agree on strength recovery but split on soreness. Here is what athletes should know.

item.title: Creatine for athletes: what the research shows
item.description: What creatine monohydrate does in muscle, what the International Society of Sports Nutrition concluded, and what is still unproven for recovery.
